QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_20

question.text: When an SIA cannot ethically or practically randomise assignment (e.g., life-saving healthcare for tribal children), which family of methods should be considered next, before falling back to pre-post comparisons?

answer.text: Strict compliance audit of Section 135 CSR spending
Quasi-experimental designs — DiD, regression discontinuity, propensity score matching, synthetic control
SEBI-mandated mandatory disclosures under LODR Regulation 33

explanation.text: The Logic: When randomisation is infeasible (ethical, legal, or operational reasons), quasi-experimental designs are the next rung on the evidence ladder: DiD, regression discontinuity (RDD), propensity score matching (PSM), synthetic control. These approximate a counterfactual using observational data before resorting to weaker pre-post. The Trap: Storytelling alone is anecdote, not evidence. CSR audit and LODR disclosures are regulatory, not causal-inference methods. Cross-Exam Context: X-A IA refers to quasi-experimental evidence in policy evaluation; XV Research Analyst uses natural experiments. XXIII requires the SIA to know the evidence hierarchy. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Publish an 'evidence ladder' in your engagement report — RCT (highest) → Quasi-experimental → Pre-post with control → Pre-post → Cross-sectional — so readers know the strength of the causal claim you're signing off.
